text:
**Likely yes, but the loss is not yet corroborated.** Satellite data detected 13.5 hectares of tree-cover loss in 2025, about 3.9% of the property. Uruguay’s 2021 forest map classified 13.1 hectares of the affected area as native forest, and the JRC map classified 98% of the event area as forest in 2020.

The evidence therefore indicates native forest loss, but the tool’s corroboration rule also requires an observation in a later year. No later year was available, so the event remains uncorroborated.
